name: George III of Great Britain
role: King of Great Britain and Ireland (1760–1820)
summary: George III was a devout Anglican monarch who defended the Crown's prerogatives, notably in choosing ministers. He insisted on suppressing the American rebellion and refused Catholic emancipation in 1801, citing his coronation oath. Much of his reign's policy was made by ministers, so few positions are recorded as his own.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: treated the American rising as treason to be suppressed (Proclamation of 1775); he did not state a general rule on revolution.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Reigned as hereditary monarch for sixty years and personally defended Crown prerogatives, including choosing ministers (1783) and refusing Catholic emancipation (1801) as bound by his coronation oath.

right-to-secede.rationale: Declared the colonies in 'open and avowed rebellion', ordering officers to suppress it and bring the rebels to justice; opposed American independence until 1782-83.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Personally chose and dismissed ministers: used his own influence against Fox's India Bill and dismissed the Fox-North ministry (1783), appointed Pitt, and forced the Grenville ministry out in 1807; the army was formally his, though he mostly deferred to cabinet on war.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Said he would not be put in the hands of a faction, yet intervened actively in party contests (India Bill 1783, 1807 dismissal); evidence points both ways.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Issued the 1775 Proclamation for Suppressing Rebellion and Sedition against the colonies and backed the war to keep the American dominions within the empire (told the Cabinet in 1779 he was resolved to hold his dominions together).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: his 1801 letter treats the coronation oath as binding him to the fundamental maxims of the constitution, so he did not claim to be above it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Created peers rapidly in 1783-84 to support Pitt's government, using hereditary honours as an instrument of his politics.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mixed record: he accepted Parliament's role but dismissed a ministry with a Commons majority and tried to sway peers in 1783, resisting a parliamentary check on his choice of ministers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: as a hereditary king he insisted on the Royal Marriages Act 1772 to control royal marriages and the line of succession.

national-church-status.rationale: In his letter to Pitt of 1 Feb 1801 he held that his coronation oath bound him to maintain the Church of England as the established church, and refused Catholic emancipation on that ground.

notes: Slave trade stance, constitutional essays, Fortescue's Correspondence and the 1775 speech from the throne were not read in full text (Fortescue and Georgian Papers pages not reached); many nulls reflect that and that ministers made most policy. He privately accepted American independence by 1783 and told John Adams in 1785 he would meet friendship with the United States.
